key_insight: A fully differentiable graph-based implicit solver treats PDE equation systems as constraints, supporting both forward simulation and inverse estimation on unstructured grids.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce forward-modeling complexity and support parameter or source estimation in physics and engineering, including geophysical uncertainty reduction.
method: Represent discretized PDE solutions on graphs derived from unstructured grids.
Incorporate equation-system constraints into a differentiable implicit solver.
Use learnable graph coarsening to accelerate forward modeling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on linear and nonlinear evolutionary and static forward problems, coefficient estimation, right-hand-side estimation, and learnable graph coarsening, but gives no quantitative results.
watch_item: Scalability and computational savings require verification because the abstract provides no mesh sizes, runtimes, or solver-tolerance details.
paper_title: Automatic Differentiation with Constraints in Forward and Inverse Problems
